title: Soldiers of the Cross, Arise
description: Soldiers of the Cross, Arise in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: William Walsham How wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 482.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sol-diers of the Cross, a-rise, Gird you with your ar-mor bright; Might-y are your en-e-mies, Hard the bat-tle ye must fight.

lines: Soldiers of the Cross, arise,
Gird you with your armor bright;
Mighty are your enemies,
Hard the battle ye must fight.
O’er a faithless, fallen world
Raise your banner in the sky;
Let it float there wide unfurled;
Bear it onward, lift it high.
Mid the homes of want and woe,
Strangers to the living Word,
Let the Savior’s heralds go,
Let the voice of hope be heard.
Where the shadows deepest lie,
Carry truth’s unsullied ray;
Where are crimes of blackest dye,
There the saving sign display.
To the weary and the worn
Tell of realms where sorrows cease;
To the outcast and forlorn
Speak of mercy and of peace.
Guard the helpless; seek the strayed;
Comfort troubles; banish grief;
In the might of God arrayed,
Scatter sin and unbelief.
Be the banner still unfurled,
Still unsheathed the Spirit’s Sword,
Till the kingdoms of the world
Are the kingdom of the Lord.

licence: Public domain: William Walsham How died in 1897.
credits: Words by William Walsham How (1823–1897), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
